operation: Error exit: stop current program sequence, put processor in idle mode, set Exit Mode and Idle Mode flags in Background Port Status (BPS) register; 6-bit jk (=0) entered into BPS.
notes: Encoded 000000 (i ignored, CAL writes 0). err is simply the jk=0 exit.

operation: Normal exit: stop program sequence, idle mode, set Exit Mode and Idle Mode flags in BPS; the 6-bit jk value (exp) is entered into the BPS register as an exit code.
notes: 'exit' with no operand = 000001 (jk=1). jk is 6 bits (j high 3, k low 3). i ignored. BPS bit positions of the code/flags are not documented in HR-2000. Restart P value after exit not documented.

operation: 1985: executes as 000xjk (exit with code jk; jk=0 behaves as error exit).
notes: CAL does not generate 001 in 1985. CONFLICT: June-1989 HR-02000-0D p.3-4 redefines 001xxx as 'CMR - Hold issue on memory busy' (see separate entry).

operation: 1989 revision only: hold instruction issue until Common Memory activity (memory busy) clears (a memory-ordering barrier). No other semantics documented.
notes: From HR-02000-0D (June 1989) page 3-4 (PDF p.44, visually verified). In the May-1985 manual 001 executes as 000. Exact completion condition not described.

operation: Register jump with return: new P <- (Ak) (32-bit parcel address, relative to BA); Ai <- parcel address of the next instruction in the current sequence (old P+1).
notes: Encoded 002ixk (j ignored). This is the subroutine call/return mechanism: call with 'r,A7 A6', return with 'j A7'. Ak is read before Ai is written.

operation: Register jump: P <- (Ak); because i=k the return address (old P+1) is written into Ak ('value in ak erased').
notes: Encoded 002kxk, i.e. i==k. Same opcode as r,Ai Ak with i=k.

Branch target is a 32-bit PARCEL address (= relative word address*4 + parcel 0..3) assembled as (m1<<16)|m2, m1 read first (3.2, lines 1704-1710, page 3-2); relative to BA (2.1.4).  1989 doc: CAL forces a parcel address; word-address expressions not allowed.

operation: Atomic test-and-set on this processor's assigned semaphore flag: if flag CLEAR -> jump to (m1<<16)|m2; in all cases the flag is set afterward. BPS semaphore bit set if flag changed 0->1.
notes: Taken branch == lock acquired. i,j,k ignored (004xxx). The flag used is the one the BPS register points to (assigned by OS per job; 8 flags in the background system, 2.1.3). Branch target is a 32-bit PARCEL address (= relative word address*4 + parcel 0..3) assembled as (m1<<16)|m2, m1 read first (3.2, lines 1704-1710, page 3-2); relative to BA (2.1.4). Not-taken: execution continues at P+3.

operation: Atomic: if semaphore flag SET -> jump to (m1<<16)|m2; flag is set afterward in all cases (so fall-through means it was clear and is now owned). BPS semaphore bit set if flag changed 0->1.
notes: Spin-lock idiom: 'L jss L' falls through when acquired. Branch target is a 32-bit PARCEL address (= relative word address*4 + parcel 0..3) assembled as (m1<<16)|m2, m1 read first (3.2, lines 1704-1710, page 3-2); relative to BA (2.1.4). Not-taken: execution continues at P+3.

operation: Set this processor's semaphore flag unconditionally; BPS semaphore bit set if previous state was 0.
notes: Used by OS to restore semaphore on job restart. 006xxx.

operation: Clear this processor's semaphore flag unconditionally; BPS semaphore bit cleared.
notes: Issues immediately but the FOLLOWING instruction does not issue until the Common Memory quadrant buffers are clear (all prior CM writes complete) - i.e. a release barrier. 007xxx.

Not-taken: execution continues at P+3. Sign test on 32-bit A; HR-2000 does not say whether zero counts as positive (Cray convention: sign-bit test, so 0 is positive).

operation: VM <- 0; then for e in 0..VL-1: VM bit (63-e) <- 1 if Vk[e] satisfies element == 0.

notes: Encoded 030xxk. Bit 2^63 corresponds to element 0. Bits for e >= VL remain 0 (VM cleared first). operation: Compressed iota: mask M = Sj (64 bits), stride s = low 32 bits of Sk; iota element n = n*s (n = 0..63). Scanning mask bits from 2^63 (n=0) down to 2^0 (n=63), each n whose mask bit is 1 delivers n*s to the next element of Vi (Vi[0], Vi[1], ...). Result length = popcount(Sj).
notes: Execution time variable (stops when remaining mask bits are zero). NOT documented: interaction with VL (whether VL limits or is updated), width and sign-extension of the accumulated n*s (unknown; a 64-bit accumulation of the sign-extended 32-bit stride is a guess), contents of Vi elements beyond popcount (assume unchanged). Both scalars captured at issue.
